cards.text: Jeremiah, the LORD's prophet to Judah, tells us the LORD gave him a new assignment. And friend, this one comes with an ADDRESS, which is more than I had in the back of that junk drawer. Go stand at the gate of the people in Jerusalem.

cards.question: The LORD sends Jeremiah to stand at the gate of the people in Jerusalem. Who goes in and out through that gate?
True or false: The LORD tells Jeremiah to stand at the gate of the people and nowhere else.

cards.text: So this isn't one speech, friend, it's a TOUR, gate after gate after gate. And the LORD hands him the opening line: 'Hear the word of the LORD, O kings of Judah, all people of Judah and Jerusalem who enter through these gates.'
Then the message starts: 'This is what the LORD says: Take heed for yourselves.' That's not small talk, friend, that's the LORD saying LISTEN UP.

cards.question: The LORD's warning is about the gates of Jerusalem on the Sabbath day. What must the people not do there?
True or false: The LORD's rule about carrying loads on the Sabbath only covers the city gates, not people's houses.
No loads and no work on the Sabbath. Instead, the LORD says, 'you must keep the Sabbath day ___'
True or false: The LORD says this Sabbath command is brand new, something the people's forefathers never heard.
The LORD gave this same Sabbath command to the people's forefathers. How did the forefathers respond?

answers.text: They wrote it on the gates

cards.text: They 'stiffened their necks' and would not receive His discipline. That's the driver whose GPS says 'recalculating' fifteen times in a row, and he just keeps going STRAIGHT.
Then the LORD lays out two roads, and He starts with the good one. 'If, however, you listen carefully to Me,' no loads through the gates on the Sabbath, keep the day holy and do no work on it.

cards.question: True or false: If the people keep the Sabbath day holy, the LORD says kings and princes will ride through the gates of Jerusalem.
On the good road, the kings who ride through Jerusalem's gates will sit on the throne of ___.
On that same good road, how long does the LORD say Jerusalem will be inhabited?

cards.text: People come from all over: the cities of Judah, the places around Jerusalem, the land of Benjamin, the foothills, the hill country and the Negev. I'm out of breath just READING the list, and they're all headed for the house of the LORD.

cards.question: On the good road, people come from all over Judah to the house of the LORD. What are they bringing?

cards.text: Then the other road, and friend, this is the part of the movie where the music changes. If they don't listen to Him and keep the Sabbath day holy, and the loads keep coming through Jerusalem's gates on the Sabbath, there's a cost.

cards.question: If the people won't keep the Sabbath day holy, what does the LORD say will come to Jerusalem's gates?
True or false: The LORD says the fire in Jerusalem's gates will leave the citadels of Jerusalem standing.

findings.problem: The joke compares being sent to a specific gate with not having an address in the junk drawer. The core action of the fact is being sent somewhere. The drawer line doesn't share that action, so the comparison doesn't click right away and a reader could say "huh?"

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The wrong answers "brief" and "open" don't read as believable ways to keep the Sabbath day, so "holy" stands out as the only serious option.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The setup on card 16 and the question both say the people are headed to the house of the LORD. That rules out "Taxes for the king" at once and makes "Stones for the walls" unlikely, which leaves "Offerings and sacrifices" as the obvious pick.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.
